I don't have the same worry about throwing discord links into commit msg, they don't appear to go away and even if they did in the future, I feel they would at least work for a period of time. I can break this reading from env into its own commit.

what about just ~ or -~ ?
This user doesn't have a home dir..... Arguably we should just use the systemd default though.  I think I pulled this for what nginx does, but it's been so long now I don't remember.

```If the setting is prefixed with the "-" character, a missing working directory is not considered fatal```

Might be what we want here?

I don't think you can have a user without a home dir.  I just hopped on a bmc and did 'useradd foo' and it put it in /home/foo.  I also noticed I have a bmcweb user and its home dir is /home/bmcweb.

A quick look on my distro and service account homes are all over the place.  some in /var, some in /run, some in /, some in /usr, others in /nonexistent...

Yeah, I was planning on doing

adduser --system --no-create-home

But fair, that's a problem for the future, i'll use -~
